description:
Returns one watchlist as a map of where to look: each company with how many signals
it has in the window and the strongest of them, plus when it was last scanned and
the progress of any scan in progress. It carries no signal bodies; read a company
worth a closer look with get_company_signals.

The window is the last `days` (default 30) by event date. With since_last_pull it is
instead everything recorded since the last complete since_last_pull read of this
list, which includes older events a recent scan only just found, and reaching the
last page of such a read moves that marker. with_signals_only leaves out companies
with nothing in the window.

Pages stop at `limit` companies or at a size every client can hold, whichever comes
first. Follow next_cursor to reach the whole list.

A scan's `status` moves through running and settling to completed. Settling means
the companies are done and the last signals are still being written, so read results
once it reports completed.

Cost: free — call it as often as you need.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same other arguments.

days.description: Count signals from the last this many days, by event date. Default 30, up to 365.

since_last_pull.description: Count only what was recorded since the last complete since_last_pull read. Default false.

watchlist.description: The list, by its id (wl_...) or its exact name.

with_signals_only.description: Leave out companies with nothing in the window. Default false.

name: get_watchlist
title: Get Watchlist
